Title: ViiV Healthcare (GSK) Director, Portfolio Access Optimization
Description:
ViiV Healthcare is a global specialty HIV company, the only one that is 100% focused on researching and delivering new medicines for people living with, and at risk of, HIV. ViiV is highly mission-driven in our unrelenting commitment to being a trusted partner for all people living with and affected by HIV. Our aim is to think, act, and connect differently through a focus on education on and treatment for HIV. We go to extraordinary lengths to deliver the sorts of breakthroughs, both in treatments, care solutions and communities, that really count. We go beyond the boundaries of medicine by taking a holistic approach to HIV through developing and supporting sustainable community programs and improving access to care. We are fully committed to push through every challenge until HIV/AIDS is eradicated. ViiV has played a significant part in delivering breakthroughs that have turned HIV into a manageable health condition. We offer the largest portfolio of HIV medicines available anywhere, and we continue our work to cater for the widest possible range of needs in response to the HIV epidemic.

We are aware of how much is at stake for those affected by HIV and we show up every day 100% committed to the patients. Our work culture is fast-paced, diverse, inclusive, competitive, and caring. But ViiV isn’t just somewhere to work – it’s a place to belong, an invitation to bring your very best, and a team full of impact-driven team members who are hungry to make a difference.

While we have been improving lives of HIV patients for 30 years, this is an especially exciting time to be at ViiV, as we evaluate novel approaches to treatment and prevention that could further reduce the impact of HIV on individuals and communities.  
  
Reporting to the Sr. Director, Portfolio Access Optimization, the role of **Director, Portfolio Access Optimization** will be responsible for assessing the strategic, financial, and operational direct and indirect impacts of government programs and policy changes through to driving solutions to maximize opportunities, minimize risks, and ensure compliance with program and policy requirements – particularly those related to the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). This position requires enterprise-level thinking and influence, strong strategic judgment, and the ability to lead through ambiguity. The director will serve as a subject matter expert on Medicare drug price negotiations and be a thought partner on market access direct and indirect implications of program and policy issues to proactively identify insights, manage risks and frame opportunities for the current portfolio and pipeline. This role is accountable for ViiV’s strategic and tactical preparations for price negotiations – leading cross-functional sub-teams internally (Finance, Medical, Legal, External Affairs, Government Relations), managing external vendor strategic projects, and facilitating overall readiness for comprehensive data packages, successful negotiations and implementation readiness.

This role is based at ViiV Healthcare’s U.S. headquarters in Durham, NC and follows a hybrid working model, requiring a minimum of 2 days per week onsite. Candidates who do not currently live within commuting distance of Durham will be required to relocate to North Carolina. This role is eligible for a domestic relocation package.Check out this link to learn more about the thriving, diverse, and cutting edge RTP area!

**Research Triangle Park | Where People + Ideas Converge (rtp.org)**

**Responsibilities**  
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following:

  

* Lead the preparation and scenario planning for CMS product negotiations
* Develop strategies for ViiV drugs selected (or at risk of selection) for the Medicare Maximum Fair Price (MFP) negotiation program
* Lead cross functional teams to ensure preparedness for any ViiV products selected for negotiations. Facilitate negotiation process and guide cross-functional teams to optimize outcomes and ensure compliance with government requirements.
* Compile and validate required data packages for drugs selected for negotiation
* Oversee framework and scenario planning for evaluating selection risk of current and pipeline assets
* Identify IRA-driven reasonable assumptions and forecast risks and partner cross-functionally within and outside of Market Access on risk mitigation strategies including but not limited to evidence generation, counteroffer strategic planning, life cycle planning, and pipeline considerations
* Be the subject matter expert on the implications and timelines of IRA implementation and its long-term impact, raising organizational acumen and preparedness.
* Manage the iterative communication loop with CMS, including reviewing initial Maximum Fair Price (MFP) offers, preparing data-driven counteroffers, and coordinating internal senior leader reviews and approvals
* Hire, lead and manage vendor relationships with external thought partners and consultants. Lead strategic projects with external vendors to identify insights as the external environment evolves and embed those insights organizationally to optimize work product
* Demonstrate superior interpersonal skills with ability to lead, influence, and gain alignment both cross-functionally and with senior leadership
* Set priorities and provide clear recommendations in complex and ambiguous circumstances
* Proactively identify and resolve/remove challenges/barriers as it relates to successful execution of business objectives and escalate in a timely fashion as needed.
* Identify US and Global direct and indirect impacts and coordinate across teams to ensure impacts are well managed
* Maintain and evolve fit-for-purpose ways of working and agile cross-functional processes

**Why You?**
============

**Basic Qualification**  
We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals:

  

* Bachelor’s degree and 5+ years of pharmaceutical, biotechnology, payer, and consulting experience OR healthcare experience
* 3+ years' experience in market access, federal policy, consulting, or similar experience
* Experience leading cross-functional initiatives.
* Experience developing executive-level presentations and recommendations.

**Preferred Qualification**  
If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus:

  

* Advanced degree in business, public health, health economics, pharmacy, public policy, or related discipline.
* 5+ years of US-based pharmaceutical industry experience in Market Access
* Extensive experience facilitating and managing effective cross-functional project teams, plans and deliverables including expertise in managing project risks, ensuring that the risks are appropriately identified, measured, managed, and communicated.
* Proven problem-solving and analytical skills with the ability to understand both data (quantitative) and market research (qualitative) results, draw conclusions, and make decisions at pace
* Strong communication, and leadership skills, with ability to synthesize and succinctly communicate complex information and insights effectively.
* Experience presenting to, communicating with, and influencing senior leadership.
* Understanding of corporate finance fundamentals (gross & net sales, P&L inputs, gross margin, COGs, working capital, etc.)
* Experience with doing or partnering on financial modelling and impact assessments.
* An understanding of current healthcare and biopharmaceutical industry issues and public and private payer reimbursement dynamics. Deep functional knowledge of Medicare policy, the IRA, and IRA implementation frameworks.
* Evidence of proactive initiative with the ability to be a self-starter, operate independently and handle multiple projects with a high degree of accountability and without significant oversight.
* Prior/demonstrated project management skills, including effective prioritization and managing several projects at one time
* Strong interpersonal skills required with proven ability to develop and maintain trusted relationships, work well in cross-functional teams, and to lead & influence complex projects across matrixed organizations (including influencing without authority)
* Proven ability to translate strategic direction into action plans, manage competing priorities, and foster organizational alignment under tight timelines.
* Experience hiring, working with and managing third-party vendors and consultants
* Demonstrated learning agility with a high level of curiosity and motivation to manage complexity and solve problems in ambiguous environments.
* Experience in or understanding of the HIV therapeutic area

**Skills**

Data to Insights, Digital Fluency, Market Access Strategies, Matrix Leadership, Payer Evidence, Pricing Strategies, Scientific Literacy

Please visit GSK US Benefits Summary to learn more about the comprehensive benefits program ViiV offers US employees. All ViiV employees receive the same benefits options and plans as GSK employee.

**Why Us?**

At ViiV Healthcare, we will not rest until we leave no person living with HIV behind. Until the 40 million people living with HIV is down to zero, we will continue searching for new ways to limit the impact of HIV.

We are the only pharmaceutical company solely focused on combating, preventing, and ultimately eradicating HIV and AIDS. At ViiV Healthcare, we do things differently. Born out of a partnership between GSK and Pfizer in 2009, with Shionogi joining in 2012, we are determined to help end the HIV epidemic. We are guided by our mission to leave no person living with HIV behind and it is this mission that unites our employees located across the globe. We combine expertise in research, manufacturing, policy and more to push the boundaries of what people think is possible in HIV treatment and care. As a result of our connection with GSK, we are able to draw on their proud history and resources. This means that you would receive all the employee benefits offered by GSK.

Living our mission of leaving no person living with HIV behind means keeping inclusion and diversity at the heart of everything we do - from our breakthrough innovation, to our diverse portfolio of medicines as well as the work we do to partner with HIV communities.

Having a truly inclusive culture where we’re all able to be ourselves and feel like we belong will make us an even stronger team, better able to perform as a business and deliver on our mission to leave no person living with HIV behind.

Title: Executive Director of Facilities and Operations
Description:
**Job Title:** Executive Director of Facilities and Operations **Exemption Status/Test:** Exempt/Executive\*

**Reports to:** Superintendent

**Dept./School:** Operations

**Primary Purpose:**
====================

Responsible for the overall management, strategic planning, development, evaluation, and implementation of district maintenance, child nutrition, warehousing, and transportation functions.

**Qualifications:**
===================

Education/Certification:

Bachelor’s degree, Masters Preferred

Special Knowledge/Skills:

Knowledge of operations management

Ability to interpret data and evaluate maintenance and custodial programs

Ability to manage budget and personnel

Ability to implement policy and procedures

Excellent communication, public relations, and interpersonal skills

**Major Responsibilities and Duties:**
======================================

**Operations Management**
-------------------------

* Oversee the management of facilities maintenance, warehouse, child nutrition, and transportation operations of the district.
* Incorporate district-level goals into operational objectives to ensure that students arrive at school and school activities safely and on time; receive nutritious meals; and attend school in an environment that is safe, clean, and conducive to learning.
* Monitor and reevaluate operations departments on an ongoing basis to ensure that district needs are being met in an effective and efficient manner. Implement changes where appropriate.
* Collaborate with architects and consultants during the design and planning phases of all construction projects to ensure compliance with the district’s specifications, design and construction standards, and building programs. Monitor the progress and compliance of ongoing construction projects.
* Ensure that the necessary time, resources, materials, and technology to support accomplishment of department goals are available.

**Policy, Reports, and Law**
----------------------------

* Implement federal and state laws and regulations and local board policy and ensure compliance. Stay abreast of state and federal public policy changes that could impact the district.
* Compile, maintain, and file all reports, records, and other documents as required.

**Budget**
----------

* Develop and administer the department budget based on documented needs and ensure that operations are cost effective and funds are managed prudently.

**Communication**
-----------------

* Ensure that established goals and expectations related to district operations are communicated clearly, consistently, and in a timely manner.

**Personnel Management**
------------------------

* Prepare, review, and revise job descriptions in maintenance, child nutrition, warehouse, and transportation departments as needed.
* Evaluate job performance of employees to ensure effectiveness.
* Select, train, evaluate, and supervise staff and make recommendations relative to assignment, retention, discipline, and dismissal.

**Safety**

* Ensure that safety standards are maintained in conformance with federal, state, and insurance regulations and a district-wide preventive safety program is developed and implemented.
* Follow district safety protocols and emergency procedures.

**Other**

* Prepare and deliver written and oral presentations on operational issues to the board. Attend regular meetings of the board.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**
=================================

Supervise, evaluate, and recommend the hiring and firing of maintenance, transportation, warehouse, and food service supervisors and staff, and operations department clerical staff.\*

**Mental Demands/Physical Demands/Environmental Factors:**
==========================================================

**Tools/Equipment Used:** Standard office equipment including personal computer and peripherals

**Posture:** Prolonged sitting; occasional bending/stooping, pushing/pulling, and twisting

**Motion:** Repetitive hand motions, frequent keyboarding and use of mouse; occasional reaching

**Lifting:** Occasional light lifting and carrying (less than 15 pounds)

**Environment:** Frequent districtwide travel; occasional statewide travel; occasional outside work with exposure to extreme hot and cold temperatures, dust, noise, vibration, and chemical and electrical hazards

**Mental Demands:** Work with frequent interruptions; maintain emotional control under stress

Title: Project Manager / Superintendent - Land Clearing & Tree Removal
Description:
**Project Manager / Superintendent – Land Clearing & Tree Removal Position****:**
=================================================================================

**Reports To:** Operations Manager / Company Ownership

**Employment Type:** Full-Time

**Location:** Indianapolis, Indiana

**Position Overview**

The Project Manager / Superintendent is responsible for the successful planning, coordination, supervision, and execution of land clearing, tree removal, forestry, and vegetation management projects. This individual will oversee day-to-day ﬁeld operations, manage crews and equipment, coordinate subcontractors, communicate with customers and project owners, and ensure projects are completed safely, efficiently, on schedule, and within budget.

The ideal candidate is an experienced leader with a strong background in land clearing, tree removal, forestry operations, heavy equipment, and construction project management. This person must be capable of managing multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining accountability for productivity, quality of work, labor costs, equipment utilization, and overall project proﬁtability.

The Project Manager / Superintendent is expected to take ownership of assigned projects and serve as the primary link between the company's office, ﬁeld personnel, customers, general contractors, engineers, and project owners.

**Primary Responsibilities**
============================

**1. Project Planning & Management**

* Review project plans, speciﬁcations, bid documents, contracts, and scopes of work before mobilization.
* Develop project schedules, work plans, production goals, and equipment requirements.
* Coordinate project mobilization, demobilization, and material disposal.
* Establish daily, weekly, and overall project objectives.
* Monitor project progress and proactively address scheduling issues, delays, and unforeseen conditions.
* Manage multiple projects and prioritize resources based on company needs.
* Identify additional work opportunities, change orders, and potential scope changes.
* Maintain accurate project records, daily reports, photographs, and documentation.
* Ensure all contract requirements and project speciﬁcations are being met.

**2. Field Supervision & Crew Management**
==========================================

* Provide direct supervision and leadership to ﬁeld crews, foremen, equipment operators, and laborers.
* Conduct regular jobsite visits to monitor progress, productivity, safety, and quality.
* Establish clear expectations and hold employees accountable for performance.
* Coordinate daily assignments and ensure crews understand the scope and priorities of their work.
* Monitor crew production and identify opportunities to improve efficiency.
* Address employee performance issues and provide coaching when necessary.
* Ensure proper staffing and labor allocation for each project.
* Maintain professional working relationships with employees, customers, and other contractors.

**3. Equipment & Fleet Management**
===================================

* Coordinate the assignment and utilization of company equipment, including forestry mulchers, excavators, dozers, skid steers, loaders, chippers, grinders, trucks, and other support equipment.
* Ensure equipment is properly allocated to maximize productivity and minimize downtime.
* Monitor equipment condition and coordinate preventative maintenance and repairs.
* Communicate equipment problems and maintenance needs to the appropriate personnel.
* Plan equipment transportation, trucking, and mobilization requirements.
* Monitor equipment utilization and identify opportunities to reduce unnecessary operating costs.
* Ensure equipment is being operated properly and efficiently.

**4. Job Costing & Financial Management**
=========================================

* Monitor project labor, equipment, fuel, trucking, subcontractor, and material disposal costs.
* Compare actual project costs and production against estimated budgets.
* Identify projects that are falling behind ﬁnancially or operationally and implement corrective measures.
* Monitor production rates and ensure crews are meeting expected performance levels.
* Review labor hours, equipment hours, and daily production reports.
* Identify opportunities to improve project proﬁtability.
* Assist with monthly job cost reviews and project ﬁnancial reporting.
* Communicate potential cost overruns, delays, and additional expenses to management.
* Verify completed work and assist with progress billing and ﬁnal invoicing.

**5. Customer & Contractor Relations**
======================================

* Serve as the primary point of contact for customers, general contractors, project owners, engineers, and inspectors on assigned projects.
* Maintain professional and consistent communication throughout the project.
* Attend preconstruction meetings, progress meetings, and jobsite coordination meetings.
* Address customer concerns and resolve issues in a timely and professional manner.
* Communicate project updates, scheduling changes, and anticipated completion dates.
* Identify additional work opportunities and communicate them to management.
* Maintain strong relationships that encourage repeat business and future opportunities.

**6. Safety & Regulatory Compliance**
=====================================

* **Make jobsite safety a top priority and ensure employees follow company safety policies and procedures**
  =========================================================================================================
* **Conduct or coordinate jobsite safety meetings and toolbox talks.**
  ====================================================================

* Identify potential hazards associated with tree removal, heavy equipment, steep slopes, overhead utilities, traffic, and environmental conditions.
* Ensure employees are properly trained and qualiﬁed for their assigned responsibilities.
* Ensure appropriate PPE and safety equipment are being used.
* Monitor compliance with OSHA regulations, traffic control requirements, environmental permits, and project-speciﬁc safety requirements.
* Stop unsafe work practices and immediately address hazardous conditions.
* Ensure all accidents, incidents, and near misses are properly reported and documented.

**7. Scheduling & Communication**
=================================

* Coordinate daily and weekly schedules with foremen, equipment operators, trucking companies, subcontractors, and management.
* Monitor weather conditions and evaluate their impact on project schedules and site accessibility.
* Communicate schedule changes and operational needs in a timely manner.
* Coordinate material hauling, disposal sites, trucking availability, and other logistical requirements.
* Keep management informed of project status, manpower requirements, equipment needs, and potential problems.
* Provide regular updates on completed work and remaining work.

**8. Quality Control & Project Closeout**
=========================================

* Ensure all work is completed according to contract speciﬁcations, project plans, and customer expectations.
* Conduct inspections of completed work and identify deﬁciencies requiring correction.
* Coordinate punch-list items and ﬁnal cleanup.
* Verify quantities and completed work before submitting billing documentation.
* Ensure project documentation, photographs, and required reports are complete.
* Coordinate ﬁnal customer walkthroughs and project closeout.

**Qualiﬁcations & Experience**
==============================

* Minimum of 3–5 years of experience in land clearing, tree removal, forestry, site preparation, or heavy construction operations.
* Previous experience managing construction projects, supervising ﬁeld crews, or serving as a foreman or superintendent.
* Strong understanding of heavy equipment and land clearing operations.
* Knowledge of tree removal, forestry mulching, brush mowing, grubbing, stump removal, material processing, and disposal operations.
* Ability to read and interpret construction plans, speciﬁcations, contracts, and project documents.
* Experience with job costing, production tracking, labor management, and equipment utilization.
* Strong organizational, communication, and leadership skills.
* Ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines.
* Proﬁciency with computers, email, spreadsheets, and project management software.
* Valid driver's license and ability to travel to multiple jobsites.
* CDL is preferred but not required.

**Personal Characteristics & Expectations** The successful candidate must demonstrate:

**Leadership:** Ability to lead crews, earn respect, and hold employees accountable.

**Accountability:** Takes ownership of projects and follows through on commitments.

**Organization:** Can manage multiple projects, schedules, employees, and equipment simultaneously.

**Problem Solving:** Able to make sound decisions and resolve ﬁeld problems without constant direction.

**Communication:** Keeps management, customers, and ﬁeld personnel informed.

**Financial Awareness:** Understands that productivity, labor hours, equipment costs, and efficiency directly affect proﬁtability.

**Initiative:** Identiﬁes problems before they become major issues and takes action to resolve them.

**Professionalism:** Represents the company in a positive and professional manner.

**Performance Expectations & Measurements**
===========================================

The Project Manager / Superintendent will be evaluated based on the following:

* Projects completed on schedule and within established budgets.

* Overall project proﬁtability and job cost performance.

* Crew productivity and production rates.

* Effective utilization of company equipment and personnel.

* Safety performance and compliance with company policies.

* Quality of completed work and customer satisfaction.

* Accurate and timely project reporting and documentation.

* Ability to manage multiple projects with minimal oversight.

* Effective communication with management, customers, and ﬁeld employees.

* Ability to identify additional work opportunities and improve operational efficiency.

**Overall Objective of the Position**
=====================================

The Project Manager / Superintendent is responsible for making sure assigned projects are completed safely, efficiently, proﬁtably, and to the satisfaction of the customer.

This individual must be a hands-on leader who understands both the ﬁeld operations and business side of land clearing and tree removal. The expectation is that they will take full ownership of their projects, anticipate problems, manage resources effectively, and deliver results without requiring constant supervision from company ownership.
